definition: In machine learning, the radial basis function kernel, or RBF kernel, is a popular kernel function used in various kernelized learning algorithms.
details: In particular, it is commonly used in support vector machine classification. An equivalent definition involves a parameter γ = 1 2 σ 2 {\displaystyle \textstyle \gamma ={\tfrac {1}{2\sigma ^{2}}}} : K ( x , x ′ ) = exp ⁡ ( − γ ‖ x − x ′ ‖ 2 ) {\displaystyle K(\mathbf {x} ,\mathbf {x'} )=\exp(-\gamma \|\mathbf {x} -\mathbf {x'} \|^{2})} Since the value of the RBF kernel decreases with distance and ranges between zero (in the infinite-distance limit) and one (when x = x'), it has a ready interpretation as a similarity measure. explainer.lead: The RBF kernel is a widely used kernel function that measures similarity between feature vectors by their distance. It matters because it lets algorithms handle nonlinear relationships through a kernelized formulation.

tiers.eli5: It gives two points a similarity score that is high when they are close together and low when they are far apart.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers plug it into support vector machine classification and other kernelized learners, tuning the width parameter sigma. A pitfall is poor sigma choice, which overfits or smooths away structure.
tiers.paperLevel: For x, x' in R^k, K(x, x') = exp(-||x - x'||^2 / (2 sigma^2)), where ||x - x'||^2 is the squared distance. Its behavior depends on the sigma parameter.

explainer.example: In an SVM classifier, two feature vectors a short distance apart receive a kernel value near 1, while distant vectors receive values near 0.
